prose_updates.tldr: Short-panel ATT identification is valid on the union of conditional parallel trends and a full-rank group-level synthetic-control mean restriction, but an analyst cannot choose the efficient influence law branch by branch when the valid restriction is unknown. Profiling the missing treated counterfactual change leaves a PT normal of rank at most \(J-1\), while profiling the full-rank SC mean restriction leaves an SC normal of rank at most \(T-J\). Their affine intersection yields a sharp local convolution lower bound computed by finite covariance-weighted programs, and observable Gram discrepancies characterize oracle adaptation. The equal-share three-group witness makes the efficiency cost strict; the single-donor and saturated-donor reductions recover the PT and SC oracle endpoints. The branch-chart extensions are definitions used to formulate a negative result: finite-coordinate splicing makes one uniformly chartwise asymptotic-linear expansion, and therefore the requested one-step, variance, and multiplier attainment theorem, false over the frozen local-sequence class.

project_justification.fill: The project derives the profiled PT and SC normal spans, solves their affine intersection by stratum covariance-weighted quadratic programs, characterizes simultaneous and one-sided oracle adaptation, supplies a strict three-group region, and proves the single-donor and saturated-donor endpoint reductions. The resulting envelope is a sharp local lower-bound benchmark for union-regular procedures, not an implemented standard error. The frozen branch-switching sequence class cannot support the requested uniform one-step and multiplier theorem because it is closed under arbitrary finite-coordinate splicing; no affirmative sequencewise continuation theorem remains in the retained graph.

prose_updates.related_work: SunXieZhang2025 is the identification anchor. Its PT condition is the donor-by-donor conditional final-change equality. Its SC hypothesis uses covariate-indexed weights common across every period, requires the weights to sum to one, permits negative weights, and assumes \(T\ge J\); the intercept row of \(B\) encodes the sum constraint. Its identification theorem does not itself require uniqueness. Its SC estimation theorem assumes a uniformly nonsingular reference-donor difference system \(M^{\prime}M\), which is equivalent after eliminating a reference donor to full column rank of the augmented matrix \(B\). The present model is a regular finite-support, uniform-overlap, uniform-moment, full-rank subclass of that identification model and matches its regular SC estimation class after reparameterization. SunXieZhang2025, Theorems 2--4, provide separate maintained-branch limit and multiplier laws; the present union envelope adds a sharp local lower-bound benchmark but does not replace those variances or furnish implemented inference. ChenSantAnnaXie2025 supplies covariance-optimal PT weighting, while the present PT geometry starts from all treated-versus-donor equalities and obtains donor-centering normals by profiling the latent treated change. TchetgenTchetgenRobinsRotnitzky2010 studies a different finite-support union model. SantAnnaZhao2020 supplies the two-group panel-DiD gradient recovered by the single-donor reduction. NeweyRobins2018, ChernozhukovChetverikovKato2016, and DukesVansteelandtWhitney2024 are guidance only for a possible repaired theorem with genuinely uniform neighborhoods, common score and remainder bounds, and no finite-coordinate replacement. Lower-bound and impossibility conclusions transfer to estimators regular over the broader published PT-or-SC union by restriction to this subclass; sharpness is local only to the stated finite-support, uniform-margin, full-rank subclass. RummoEtAl2026 and the Alaska analysis in SunXieZhang2025 motivate the lower-bound diagnostic but receive no new standard-error procedure from this paper.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proved deliverables are the intersection tangent-normal characterization, the finite covariance-weighted union convolution lower bound, the oracle-adaptation Gram tests, the strict three-group witness, and the single-donor and saturated-donor endpoint reductions. The bound is sharp in the stated local tangent experiment and transfers as a lower bound to procedures regular over the broader published union by restriction, but sharpness is claimed only for the regular finite-support, uniform-margin, full-rank subclass. The frozen local-sequence class makes a single uniformly chartwise asymptotic-linear expansion, and hence the requested one-step, variance-consistency, and multiplier-coverage theorem, false by finite-coordinate splicing. The branch-chart extensions are definitions used in that obstruction. No positive sequencewise continuation theorem remains; the obstruction merely does not rule one out under additional uniform-neighborhood and common-remainder assumptions.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The union envelope is a local regularity lower bound at fixed-rank intersection laws. It is not an attaining estimator, a usable standard error, or a multiplier-confidence procedure. The negative theorem applies to the frozen sequence class because arbitrary finite-coordinate replacements defeat uniformity; it does not settle a redesigned sequence class with one common neighborhood and common QMD and remainder bounds. Rank failure, vanishing overlap, changing covariate support, covariance degeneracy, and weight-boundary restrictions require different local experiments.
